Apple Podcasts has long been my go-to podcast app, but its core "Up Next" queue feature has a significant flaw. I'm excited to share that iOS 27.2 finally brings a fix.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" queue into two sections: New Episodes and Continue Listening

There's a lot to love about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that make this app my go-to. I also love all the recent video-related upgrades.

However, for years the core "Up Next" queue feature in Apple Podcasts has kept making me consider switching to other apps.

I previously wrote about why "Up Next" feels difficult to use. To briefly summarize:

  • It can be hard to clearly see which podcasts are available to listen to
  • Episodes easily go missing, and even ones you've already started listening to can be hard to keep track of

However, I'm thrilled to share that iOS 27.2 brings a long-overdue fix to "Up Next." The solution is to split the feature into two separate sections:

  • New Episodes
  • Continue Listening

At the very top of the app is "New Episodes," which looks similar to "Up Next" and works in largely the same way. Just as the name suggests, it only shows the latest episode of every show you follow.

"Continue Listening" sits right below it, serving as a central hub where you can place all the episodes you've already started but haven't finished.

Together, these two sections address the biggest issues I had with the "Up Next" queue feature.

I can see all the new content at a glance, and I no longer have to worry about losing track of episodes, because any episode I've started can be found in "Continue Listening." There are still some minor issues, but these changes alone have already solved my main problems with "Up Next."

If it's been a while since you've tried Apple Podcasts, iOS 27.2 is a great time to give it another go.

Do you use Apple or another podcast app? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
